propositions: Compaction worker mutations (SNAPSHOT write, *.retired renames, .archived deletions) before git commit with no rollback on worker death leave the worktree dirty, causing git merge to abort and stranding local commits off origin (data-loss risk).
Tracked runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) committed before gitignore patterns existed are never un-tracked, causing marker churn to perpetually appear as tracked dirt in git status.
Sync reconverge fails to recover from two abort variants: untracked files origin wants to create, and tracked-file deletions/modifications (Your local changes would be overwritten).
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) traverse archived and active tickets with no scoping, causing scan cost to grow with store size rather than active working set.
Orphaned intent markers, stale locks, and regenerable worktree artifacts left by interrupted compaction folds create wedged state with no self-healing path or operator repair tooling.
Push recovery for non-fast-forward pushes lacks the same untracked-collision and tracked-deletion recovery logic available to sync reconverge.
